title: Monday Teacher Plan
note: 4 teaching days this week (Wed Oct 28 is a minimum day). Every grade turns in once, at the end of Friday's class.

4th Period.goal: By the end of class, I can explain what a factory method hides inside its closed box, and name the function and file where MY game makes its bricks.
4th Period.exitTicket: What does a factory method hide inside its closed box, and which function in your game makes your bricks?
prep: Wayground: classroom expectations quiz ready to launch
Weekly Grade Check-In form link posted on the board and Google Classroom
Video queued: The Factory Method Pattern (Train To Code, ~4 min), also linked in Google Classroom
bricks.js and game.js from the base game open on the projector
Factory Pattern assignment + exit ticket posted on Google Classroom

segments.title: Wayground: classroom expectations
segments.do: Launch the expectations Wayground as students walk in. Circulate and check logins.
segments.why: Maslow: a predictable start lowers anxiety and resets norms for the week.
tips: Start it before the bell so early arrivals begin right away.
Quietly help anyone stuck logging in instead of calling them out.

segments.title: Review answers + today's goal
segments.do: Go over the most-missed expectations, then read the SMART goal aloud and point to it on the board.
segments.why: Front-loading expectations and the goal is a universal support; students know exactly what 'done' looks like.
tips: Have a student rephrase the goal in their own words (ELL support).
Give think time before calling on anyone.

segments.title: Grade check: Infinite Campus + form
segments.do: Students open Infinite Campus, find their OVERALL grade in this class, and fill out the Weekly Grade Check-In form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSc7aOcYeQCYbcaK7_ulLeXIof-YKjW72hPA15cpJvm6ED1nIw/viewform?usp=header
segments.why: Self-monitoring and ownership. Emails home about failing grades go out in a week, so every student gets a fair warning and a plan first (Maslow: safety, no surprises).
tips: Post the form link on the board and Google Classroom before class.
Grades are private: no reading grades aloud, and turn screens away from neighbors.
Below 70%: they write a plan in the form. Point them to the regrade form and Tuesday tutoring (3:15–4:00).
Exit tickets can't be redone. Missing work can still be turned in late for full credit.

segments.title: This week and the points
segments.do: Walk the week: Mon find, Tue plan, Wed no class, Thu build, Fri turn in once. 85 points for every box even if the game breaks.
segments.why: Maslow safety: seeing the grading floor first makes it safe to try hard things.
tips: Say out loud: today the ONLY thing turned in is the exit ticket.
Point to the week on the handout so students can track it.

segments.title: Video + mini-lesson: the closed box
segments.do: Play the Train To Code factory method video (~4 min). Then teach the words: FACTORY METHOD, CLOSED BOX, ATTRIBUTES, INSTANCE, SELECTION LOGIC, using the video's animal example (barks → Dog; eats mice + longer than 3 ft → Snake; otherwise Cat).
segments.why: Bloom Remember/Understand: one model (the Boeing factory as a closed box) and one worked example before any code. The handout uses the video's exact words.
tips: Pause on the Boeing factory: 'What do you see from outside? What's hidden inside?'
Ask pairs: 'In the animal example, what are the attributes? What's the instance?'
Key rule: simple on the outside, selection logic hidden inside.

segments.title: I do: find where bricks are made
segments.do: On the projector, find makeBricks() in bricks.js (the inner workings), list.push({ x, y, width, height }) (each brick instance and its 4 attributes), and bricks = makeBricks(); in game.js (the outside of the closed box).
segments.why: Fully worked first round: everyone sees success before trying it in their own code.
tips: Use Ctrl + F live so they see the search move.
Remind them their game may look a little different, and that's fine.
Point out: makeBricks() hides how bricks are made, but has no selection logic yet. That's Thursday.

segments.title: You do: ask Copilot, then check it
segments.do: Students paste the question into Copilot Chat, then open the file themselves to confirm. Circulate.
segments.why: Bloom Understand: AI explains, but students verify with their own eyes. Real engineering habit.
tips: If Copilot offers to edit code, students say no. Today is find-and-explain only.
Check in first with students who struggled last week.
Early finishers: point to Future Engineer (the tiny makeBrick(x, y) factory method is the best one).

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom using a sentence frame.
segments.why: Checks the closed-box idea and the real code location, which Tuesday's Wayground reviews.
tips: Read the question and both frames aloud.
Allow dictation or speech-to-text for students who need it.
Remind: Future Engineer turns in alongside the exit ticket for 1 KB point.

watchFor: Students asking Copilot to change code today.
Codespace won't open: Code → Codespaces → reopen last week's.
Game with no bricks.js: search all files with Ctrl + Shift + F for push(.

6th Period.goal: By the end of class, I can use Duplicate and Repeat to make a row of 5 matching triangles in TinkerCAD, and explain why bridges use triangles.
6th Period.exitTicket: Why do engineers use triangles to build bridges?
prep: Wayground: classroom expectations quiz ready to launch
Weekly Grade Check-In form link posted on the board and Google Classroom
TinkerCAD open on the projector with an empty design
TinkerCAD class code on hand for sign-in problems
TinkerCAD Truss Bridge assignment + exit ticket posted

segments.title: Wayground: classroom expectations
segments.do: Launch the expectations Wayground as students walk in.
segments.why: Maslow: same routine every Monday. With 35 students, the routine is the management plan.
tips: Stand at the door and greet as they enter.
Redirect quietly and privately.

segments.title: Review answers + today's goal
segments.do: Review the most-missed expectations, then read the SMART goal aloud.
segments.why: Front-load expectations before any tech is on the screen.
tips: Ask one student to repeat the goal back.
Give think time before calling on anyone.

segments.title: Grade check: Infinite Campus + form
segments.do: Students open Infinite Campus, find their OVERALL grade in this class, and fill out the Weekly Grade Check-In form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSc7aOcYeQCYbcaK7_ulLeXIof-YKjW72hPA15cpJvm6ED1nIw/viewform?usp=header
segments.why: Self-monitoring and ownership. Emails home about failing grades go out in a week, so every student gets a fair warning and a plan first (Maslow: safety, no surprises).
tips: Post the form link on the board and Google Classroom before class.
Grades are private: no reading grades aloud, and turn screens away from neighbors.
Below 70%: they write a plan in the form. Point them to the regrade form and Tuesday tutoring (3:15–4:00).
Exit tickets can't be redone. Missing work can still be turned in late for full credit.

segments.title: This week and the points
segments.do: Mon triangles, Tue deck, Wed no class, Thu top of the bridge, Fri finish and turn in once. Whatever they have is 70 points.
segments.why: Maslow safety: knowing the floor lowers fear of starting.
tips: Say: nothing gets turned in today except the exit ticket.

segments.title: Why triangles? What a truss is
segments.do: Show the square vs. triangle table and the Warren truss diagram. Count the upward triangles together.
segments.why: Bloom Understand: the idea comes before the tool, so the clicking has a reason.
tips: Use your hands: push a square into a slant, show a triangle can't.
Say 'rigid' and have the class repeat it (ELL vocabulary).

segments.title: We do: Duplicate and Repeat
segments.do: Click along step by step: Roof shape → turn to see the triangle → Ctrl + D → drag until corners touch → Ctrl + D three more times.
segments.why: Fully worked first round, everyone builds the same thing at the same pace.
tips: Pause after each step and check thumbs up before moving on.
Most common problem: they dragged before pressing Ctrl + D. Undo to 2 triangles and redo the move.
Stand where you can see the most screens.

segments.title: You do: finish a row of 5
segments.do: Students finish their own row of 5 and check it against the 3 boxes on the handout.
segments.why: Bloom Apply: they repeat the skill on their own.
tips: Check in first with students who had sign-in trouble.
Early finishers: hollow triangles or fill the gaps (Future Engineer).

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom using a sentence frame.
segments.why: Checks the concept (why triangles), not just the clicks.
tips: Read the question and frames aloud.
Allow dictation for students who need it.

watchFor: Copies stacking: drag first, then Ctrl + D.
Copies jumping too far: Undo back to 2, move the copy again.
Sign-in problems: hand out the class code instead of troubleshooting Google.

7th Period.topic: Square vs. Triangle: the push test (cardboard)
7th Period.goal: By the end of class, my partner and I have measured, cut, and glued a cardboard square and triangle, push-tested both, then braced the square and tested it again.
7th Period.exitTicket: Which shape kept its shape when you pushed it, and what happened when you braced the square?
prep: Wayground: classroom expectations quiz ready to launch
Weekly Grade Check-In form link posted on the board and Google Classroom
Supplies out per pair: cardboard, scissors, glue, pencil, 1 sheet of paper each (measuring stick)
One bag per group + marker for first names
Pairs decided ahead of time (intentional grouping)
Warren Truss Bridge assignment + exit ticket posted

segments.title: Wayground: classroom expectations
segments.do: Launch the expectations Wayground as students walk in. Supplies stay untouched for now.
segments.why: Maslow: routine first, materials second.
tips: Say: 'Hands off the supplies until I say go.'

segments.title: Review answers + today's goal
segments.do: Review the most-missed expectations, especially material and scissor rules, then read the goal aloud.
segments.why: Front-load safety and expectations before a hands-on day.
tips: Model how scissors stay on the desk when not cutting.

segments.title: Grade check: Infinite Campus + form
segments.do: Students open Infinite Campus, find their OVERALL grade in this class, and fill out the Weekly Grade Check-In form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSc7aOcYeQCYbcaK7_ulLeXIof-YKjW72hPA15cpJvm6ED1nIw/viewform?usp=header
segments.why: Self-monitoring and ownership. Emails home about failing grades go out in a week, so every student gets a fair warning and a plan first (Maslow: safety, no surprises).
tips: Post the form link on the board and Google Classroom before class.
Grades are private: no reading grades aloud, and turn screens away from neighbors.
Below 70%: they write a plan in the form. Point them to the regrade form and Tuesday tutoring (3:15–4:00).
Exit tickets can't be redone. Missing work can still be turned in late for full credit.

segments.title: I do: measuring stick, strip, joint
segments.do: Model it: fold a sheet the long way 3 times into a measuring stick and mark the ½ crease. Trace both long edges on the cardboard for one strip, ½ stick long. Cut along the wavy layer, overlap two ends in a glue square, press and hold 30 seconds.
segments.why: Fully worked first round. Measuring and cutting is a skill they'll use all year.
tips: Show cutting across the flutes crushing the strip, then along them working.
Assign roles: Square Engineer and Triangle Engineer. Both measure and cut.
Everyone uses the same paper, so every stick matches.

segments.title: You do: build both shapes
segments.do: Square Engineer cuts 4 strips and builds the square. Triangle Engineer cuts 3 and builds the triangle. While glue sets, pairs predict out loud.
segments.why: Complex Instruction: two roles, both necessary. Bloom Apply.
tips: Check sticks first. Most errors come from sloppy folds; edges must line up before creasing.
Listen in on predictions and ask 'why?' to push reasoning.
Visual timer on the board.

segments.title: Push test, brace, test again
segments.do: Pairs push the square, then the triangle. Square Engineer lays a strip corner to corner, marks it, cuts a brace, glues it, and they test again.
segments.why: Bloom Analyze: change one variable and compare. This is the added rigor this class asked for.
tips: Don't tell them the answer. Ask: 'What did the brace turn your square into?'
Remind: push gently, we're testing shape, not breaking it.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom using a sentence frame.
segments.why: They explain the result in words, which is the heart of today's goal.
tips: Read the question and frames aloud.
Allow dictation for students who need it.

segments.title: Clean up + bag pieces
segments.do: Scraps in the bin, supplies back. Shapes go in the group bag with first names.
segments.why: Routines keep materials days possible. Their shapes come back Tuesday.
tips: Count scissors back in before the bell.
Thank specific students for good material handling.

watchFor: Cutting across the corrugation crushes strips. Cut along the flutes.
Testing before the glue sets. Give it the prediction time first.
One partner doing all the cutting. Both roles measure and cut.

accommodations: Agenda on the board, goal reviewed after the quiz, chunked numbered steps, I do before you do, check-yourself checklist, sentence frames, frequent check-ins, positive reinforcement. Get attention before directions; give them spoken, written, and shown.
Key words with a picture (ORDER/FACTORY/PRODUCT, truss diagram, strip and joint diagram). Two sentence frames per exit ticket. Partner talk before writing.
Lexend Deca handouts, large type. Read steps aloud during I do / We do. Text-to-speech and speech-to-text OK. Spelling not graded.
Short timed chunks with a visual timer. Movement built into 6th grade. Seat near the demo. If/then for non-preferred steps. Discreet redirection, fidgets, break pass.

Extended time and dictation on the exit ticket. Shortened floor: 8th finds the function only; 7th makes 3 triangles; 6th builds and tests one shape. Supportive partner. Calm-down space and trusted adult.
Future Engineer (OPTIONAL), pick one for 1 KB point.
frameworks: Each grade starts the week's product. No DONUTS vote this week: votes are only for work with real creative freedom.
Assigned roles, 'no one is good at all of this, everyone is good at some of it,' and publicly naming competence.
Predictable routine, points shown up front, one exit ticket only, the weekly grade check so no grade is a surprise, belonging through roles.
8th Remember/Understand (closed box, factory method, find it in code). 7th Understand/Apply. 6th Apply/Analyze.
